_readme: Single source of truth for the brand. Every skill, agent and script reads this file (scripts via numa_common.load_brand()). Most entries are facts: {"value": ..., "status": ..., "source": ..., "note": ...}. Prefer values whose status is 'confirmed'; never present a 'needs_katie' value as fact in public copy. The owners answered the setup questions on 2026-11-13 (docs/QUESTIONS_FOR_KATIE.md lists what is still open); their answers override research and earlier defaults (DECISIONS D25). The business name is "Numa" in every user-facing text; "NUMA" survives only in the plugin's own names (numa-studio, Drive folder and file names). People data (staff, providers, members, consent) is private: it lives in STATE/people.json (schemas/people.schema.json), never here; this file names only roles plus the co-founders. Asset and font paths are relative to the plugin root. Operational numbers (model tiers, Higgsfield prices and budget, Instagram API version, render targets, schedule) live in config/studio.json, not here.

transcript_fixes._readme: Speech-to-text corrections applied by fix_transcript.py. Each fix replaces any variant (whole word, case-insensitive unless case_sensitive is true, surrounding punctuation kept) with 'to'. When 'next_words' is set, the fix applies only if the following word is one of them. Phrases in 'protect' are never changed. The shoot-card script, when present, is the truth for spelling and wins over this list.

claims._readme: The claims policy and the brand's word rules as data. claims_scan.py, validate_plan.py and the Critic use it on ALL user-facing text: voiceover, on-screen text, slides, captions, hashtags and pinned comments. Patterns are Python regular expressions matched case-insensitively; a rule that must match case ("NUMA") uses a scoped inline flag, (?-i:...). Before scanning, phrases in 'allow_exact' and matches of 'allow_patterns' are removed (the safety line names 'blood pressure' on purpose; 'treat yourself' and 'a treat' are not medical). Each banned entry has a severity: 'fail' (exit 1, Critic hard gate) or 'warn' (a WARN line for review), and an optional kind: claim (health or comparison claim), brand (name and word rules, emojis), fact (a fact Numa must not state), offer (a private or unconfirmed offer in public copy). The owners confirmed the claims list on 2026-11-13 and chose to skip a lawyer's review; this is general information, not legal advice.

rules.text: Visuals count. No limping-in, jogging-out stories, no before/after of bodies, skin or bloodwork.
Testimonials are Numa's claims. Feature experience ("my favorite hour of the week"), never outcomes ("cured my back pain"). Never repost or pin a member's health claim.
Education stays education. Ask the DPT reels can explain what research does and doesn't show, but carry no booking pitch in the same reel, and never turn Katie's credential into a promise of results.
Titles matter. Breathwork staff are "guides" or "facilitators"; only licensed counselors talk about mental health, and only within their scope.
Safety is good content. Add the safety line on cold and heat reels; never show breath-holding in or near water.
Paid or comped creators disclose it in the video and the first line ("#ad" or "I get free sessions"). Reviews are never bought or conditioned on being positive.

The "57 minutes of sauna and 11 of cold a week" line is owner-approved, but its source isn't recorded yet (Doc 04 science table; owner: Scott). It stays out of posts until claims.dosing_line.blocked is false.
Any reel with AI-animated people or AI-generated scenes gets Instagram's AI label.
No quote cards, designed flyers or posters (Numa's flops). Member words go in the caption or over a real photo of that member.
Only Scott, Katie, instructors and staff, and members with a yes on record appear. Lead member stories with the members STATE/people.json names. A recorded "no" means never, not even blurred.
Children never appear until the owners decide (consent.children).
Never film the zones in consent.never_film.
No comparisons with competitors, named or not.
Promote only offers in brand.json, inside their dates and only when confirmed and public; never invent an offer, code or rate.

safety_line.text: Talk to your doctor first if you have a heart, blood pressure or breathing condition.

ai_processing_covered.note: The owners' answer covers posting a person's photo or words; it doesn't explicitly cover sending a face to AI motion. Until a person's yes names AI processing, no member face goes to Higgsfield.

social_posts_covered.note: Owners: covered: we ask each person before posting their photo or using their words.

children.note: Open: never, or only with a parent's yes on record? Until the owners decide: never. Kids 10 and up attend (10 to 14 with a parent); past posts showed kids with a parent's yes.

release_form.value: Each person is asked one at a time; permissions are logged in Doc 04.

process.value: We ask each person, one at a time, before we show them or use their words. Permissions are logged in Doc 04.
process.source: owners' setup answers, 2026-11-13 (Q25), owners' setup answers, 2026-11-13 (Q48)

log.note: Where Doc 04 lives is open. Until it is linked, consent.list (the _Plan Consent List) is the machine-readable copy the crew checks.

auto_post.note: The system posts on its own only after a person approves the post (human_approval_required). Nothing goes out without a person approving it.

require_approval.source: owners' setup answers, 2026-11-13 (Q34), owners' setup answers, 2026-11-13 (Q35)
require_approval.note: The approval switch is on: every post is held until a person approves it (same policy as human_approval_required; DECISIONS D26).

see_first.note: Member posts also need the member's own yes (member_yes_required). Every post is held anyway (require_approval).

legal_review_done.note: No longer needed: the owners said to skip the advertising lawyer (Q51). No lawyer reviewed the policy. Kept, set true, because post-reel still reads it as a gate; human approval (human_approval_required) replaces it.

posting.google_business_profile: Post the week's best reel there too (spec p.50).

posting_time.note: Re-tuned to Numa's own data after the first 30 reels.

posting.ai_label_rule: Switch on Instagram's AI label for any reel with AI-animated people or AI-generated scenes (spec p.22, p.50).
posting.music_rule: Numa posts as a business: never trending or popular songs. Music is Numa's own or licensed, and each reel's sources.txt records the source (spec p.19). The music source is open (ask Emma).

digest_destination.note: Open: email, text, or the Claude app? Katie and Scott read the digest now; the Studio Manager will later.

human_approval_required.note: "Nothing goes out without a person approving it." The approval mechanism is wired in the commands by a later task.

member_yes_required.note: Any post that shows a member needs that member's yes first.

approver.note: Open: who approves each post, and how (a Sheet checkbox, a reply, or a Meta Business Suite draft)? Default per D26: an Approved status on the plan Sheet row, set by the owners or Emma.

music_source.note: Open: where the music comes from (ask Emma).

email_tool.note: Open: which email tool sends member emails (where NEWBIE may appear). Mindbody is the booking system (confirmed).
